items.stem: Find the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100.
Explain how to find 1 + 2 + … + 200 quickly by pairing terms.
items.answer: Pair 1 with 200, 2 with 199, …: each pair is 201 and there are 100 pairs, so the sum is 100 × 201 = 20100.
items.markingKey: Pairing idea (R1); total (A1).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why a geometric sequence with 0 < r < 1 has terms that get smaller but never reach zero.

items.stem: Explain why €5,000 at 3% for 15 years earns more with compound interest than with simple interest, and find the difference.
items.answer: Simple: €2,250.00; compound: €2,789.84. Compound interest also earns interest on interest, so it is €539.84 more.

items.stem: Explain whether 201 is a term of the sequence 15, 20, 25, ….
items.answer: uₙ = 15 + (n − 1)5; 201 − 15 = 186, which is not a multiple of 5, so n would not be a whole number: 201 is not a term.
items.markingKey: n-th term equation set up (M1); non-integer n interpreted (R1).

items.stem: Sana has two sequences: P = 2, 6, 18, 54, … and Q = 2, 5, 8, 11, …. Explain which is geometric and which is arithmetic, and which grows faster in the long run.
items.answer: P has constant ratio 3 (geometric); Q has constant difference 3 (arithmetic). Geometric growth multiplies, so P eventually grows much faster.
items.markingKey: Both identified with reason (R1); long-term comparison (R1).

items.stem: Explain why someone who saves CHF 100 a month from age 24 usually ends up with far more at age 60 than someone who saves CHF 200 a month from age 34.
items.answer: The early saver’s money has 10 more years of compound growth; growth multiplies, so the extra years outweigh the larger later deposits (at typical rates).
items.markingKey: Compound growth over time (R1); comparison (R1).

items.stem: Explain why a value depreciating by a fixed percentage never reaches zero.
items.answer: Each year it is multiplied by a positive number less than 1, so it shrinks but stays positive.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Each year it is multiplied by a positive number less than 1, so it shrinks but stays positive. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)
